0.original: Kokkol Dankkol is, as usual, worked up over the aetherburner.

29.original: Proceed to the entrance of Thaumazein.

48.original: I did thoroughly brief Kokkol on refined adamantite's history. I only volunteered to go to the reactor because I had finished and there was little else to do.

49.original: Hopefully that dispels any misapprehensions that I was kicked out for prattling on...

50.original: <sigh> I do trust you to deliver on your promise, I do. Only...

51.original: I hate waitin'! I want that adamantite, and I want it <hex:021A020203>now<hex:021A020103>!

52.original: We...er, share your impatience, I assure you. Is there truly nothing else we can assist with in the meantime?

53.original: I wish! This sittin' about's unbearable. Pity the Forum frowns on recreational explosions...

54.original: Well, so long as they can't prove it was premeditated. Get you gone─I've mistakes to make!

55.original: ...In that case, I suppose I should go and return the key to the reactor. I'll have one more look to make sure that nothing has gone wrong. Unintentionally or otherwise.

56.original: I'm certain there are better uses for <hex:021A020203>your<hex:021A020103> time, however. I will join you in Sharlayan Hamlet anon!

57.original: Any smoke risin' from the building behind me will be entirely unrelated to what I <hex:021A020203>didn't<hex:021A020103> say, got it?

58.original: If you wait here, your companions are bound to turn up sooner or later...

60.original: I had no idea how massive a weight it was until he lifted it off my shoulders... But more importantly, his words were an affirmation that the path we walk is the right one.

61.original: A part of me might have been satisfied so long as my family and friends survived the Final Days. But to save this star is what we <hex:021A020203>all<hex:021A020103> want most, and if those same people believe that I can help see it done, who am I to say otherwise?

62.original: Come what may, I will fight for this world of ours until the very end.

63.original: If I never see another crate again, it will be too soon.

64.original: Unaided, we Scions could never have gathered such a bounty. Refined adamantite, relics sacred and ancient alike...

66.original: Lyse sent a letter along with Gridania's contribution. It seems she traveled there to aid in their adamantite recovery.

67.original: Evidently, journeying to Gridania was quite the trial. As was getting into the Dalamud shard. As was reaching its depths...

68.original: I suspect she will have few kind words to say about the Allagans when next we meet.

69.original: I cannot wait to see what our friends from the Ironworks do with the ship!

70.original: The time has come to claim our prize. Are you prepared?

71.original: I apologize for not informing you earlier of Erenville's involvement. He was something of a contingency plan.

72.original: Thank goodness we had him and his fellow gleaners to hand, though. It would have been monstrously difficult to locate Cid and transport the Hannish delegation here otherwise...

73.original: <cough> My throat hurts from directing so many people to Labyrinthos...but that only proves we got our money's worth!

74.original: We've finally managed to clear the harbor, which means the rest is in the engineers' capable hands.

75.original: Meanwhile, Father has issued to us an invitation.

76.original: As was agreed, he will reveal the means by which Hydaelyn may be contacted.

77.original: We are to meet him at Aporia when we're ready. Given the vital knowledge She holds, I suggest we leave without delay.

78.original: It transpires, however, that the Forum's method for speaking with Her is not without risks. I am curious to hear what those might entail─but regardless, be warned.

79.original: Most of those who arrived with the adamantite have offered to stay and see to any remaining tasks that need doing.

80.original: The Forum has already asked for my assistance in overseeing the process, so you needn't worry about a thing!

81.original: Thank you, Tataru. We're off to Aporia, then!

82.original: I don't want any of you getting hurt─but I do hope you'll wring as much information out of Hydaelyn as you can. For all we know, this is the one and only opportunity we'll get.

83.original: <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>. I have already shown the others inside.

84.original: You will want to speak with Clarilaine. She has the key to the lift, and can send you down after me.

85.original: You're with Master Fourchenault, yes? Just step inside the lift here.

87.original: You are welcome to use the lift whenever you like.

88.original: From here, we proceed to the heart of Labyrinthos, and its most closely guarded secret─Thaumazein.

89.original: It marks the beginning and end of our efforts─whence we delved to seek audience with the star, and whence we will embark on our journey to the heavens.

91.original: I bid you welcome to Thaumazein. Direct your attention toward its center to behold the ark over which we have long labored.

92.original: As you can see, 'twas designed as a medium-sized craft, the better to reduce fuel consumption. Miniaturizing magicks have been applied to its interior to ensure that the thrust-to-weight ratio does not place too great a limitation on its freight capacity.

93.original: The aetherburner, as you know, has been removed for further modification, but we shall reattach it soon enough.

94.original: I have received word that Kokkol and several of your allies are working on it with an intense fervor.

95.original: They are sure to see it done. 'Twas by their expertise that many a prior disaster was averted.

96.original: If anything, I fear they will not afford us much time for speaking with Hydaelyn ere they finish...

97.original: Point taken. Let us move on. I must warn you again, however, that even with the benefit of our device, to treat with Her is not a simple feat.

98.original: To think how many generations labored for this end...and that we aim higher still.

99.original: We must spare no preparation─and that means speaking with Hydaelyn, no matter the cost.

100.original: I can well imagine the zeal with which they're working on the aetherburner, and all I can say is that I'm glad we have something to do other than get in their way.

101.original: Once it's ready, we'll see to it that the ship is put to good use!

102.original: I doubt this is what Erenville meant when he said that there remains much we do not know, but I still can't believe everything that was hidden underneath the city this entire time.

103.original: 'Twould seem enchantments most advanced have been woven into the ship's very bones. Wilfsunn and Bloewyda were doubtless called upon for their expertise in teleportation magicks...

104.original: We must learn of Hydaelyn's greater plan. We can only hope that She also knows the current location of Meteion...

105.original: ...And we can do neither if we do not focus on whatever trial awaits us within.

106.original: It was the Allagans who first combined the mechanical and aetherial sciences into a revolutionary discipline.

107.original: Given that this ship is nothing short of a technological marvel in that precise vein, Allagan salvage should suit it well.

108.original: You feel it too, don't you? The ship is impressive, but it pales in comparison to the vast primordial power beneath our feet...

109.original: If meeting Hydaelyn proves difficult even for the Forum, then perhaps I─

110.original: Oh, 'tis an unformed idea at this phase, I'm afraid. I will duly inform you if anything comes of it.

111.original: I have done what I can to impress upon you the gravity of what lies ahead.
